note: Loot sources whose real mechanic is not visible in their drop rows. A watchlisted source fails the not_on_watchlist validation check and is forced to needs_review however cleanly it parses, because parsing cleanly proves nothing about a mechanic the rows do not encode. Remove an entry only when the mechanic is modelled and the simulation has been checked against the wiki's own figures.

entries.title: Reward Cart
entries.detail: Genuinely blocked on two unstated numbers, not merely a missing formula — read directly from the fetched wikitext. (1) The Logs sub-table's rows are all rarity=Varies; the prose says only that a higher Woodcutting level makes higher-tier logs more likely, with no numbers given anywhere — stated to exist, never stated, the same 'named but never quantified' shape as elsewhere on this watchlist, not a guessable rate. (2) The pyromancer outfit roll ('1/150 chance ... players have the least of', tie-broken Garb, hood, robe, boots) is a RELATIVE comparison across four item counts, a shape ownershipGate's single-count threshold cannot express. Separately, and also still unbuilt: how many rolls a run yields scales with points earned fighting the Wintertodt (lighting braziers, adding kindling, healing the pyromancer), needing the still-stub wintertodt_points formula. The warm gloves/bruma torch substitutions and the remaining uniques ARE expressible today (ordinary ownershipGate thresholds and plain fixed rates), but none of it has been built yet.

entries.title: Reward pool
entries.detail: SHIPPED per permit, not per encounter — data/overrides/reward-pool.json, 12 wiki-figure tests in apps/ingest/test/reward-pool.test.ts. The page's own unit is the permit (banked, then redeemed one at a time, resolved at the Fishing level held at redemption), and both the 6,400-slot main table and the separate nine-item rare-unique table are modelled exactly at that unit — cross-checked against the page's own '~45/80 chance to roll the fish sub-table' figure and all seven Fishing-level brackets. What stays unmodelled, and why this remains watchlisted: converting Tempoross activity points into a permit count. The page states permits start at 1 above 2,000 points and add 1 per 700 points 'with a chance at rounding up' but never gives the rounding rule, so tempoross_points stays a stub and a user supplies a permit count directly rather than a points total. Genuinely unstated, not unbuilt laziness.

entries.title: Duke Sucellus
entries.detail: Loot is a sequential roll-until-success chain described only in page prose, not in any drop row: 1/90 tradeable unique table (1/30 awakened), else 1/48 awakener's orb, else 1/25 frozen tablet, else 1/200 ice quartz, else 1/5 supply drop table, else the standard table; separately 1/2500 Baron and 1/40 clue after that. A perfect kill also gives 50% more loot from the standard table. The page's dropsline rows reconcile to a valid denominator on their own, so this source parses cleanly and would otherwise look verified — the chain order and the perfect-kill bonus are the parts that are invisible to the parser.

entries.title: Zalcano
entries.detail: Two curves the page never states. (1) Main- and tertiary-table drops "scale with the player's points" and the points themselves are defined exactly (P_M = H + 2S; P_T = min(H,400) + 2*min(S,300)), but the function turning points into loot is not on the page, so zalcano_points stays a stub and main-table quantities remain the crowd-sourced ranges. (2) The Zalcano shard is "Between 1/750 and 1/1500 depending on contribution" with no stated interpolation; the primary 1/750 is kept rather than a guessed curve. Everything else IS modelled and wiki-verified in data/overrides/zalcano.json and apps/ingest/test/zalcano.test.ts: both eligibility gates (>=5 shield damage, >=31 combined via the derived totalDamage field), the role-keyed crystal shard tier (1/2/3), MVP-only infernal ashes, the MVP's +10% rounded up (ceilDelta), and the tertiary 1/200 x 1/40 onyx split.

entries.title: Chest (Tombs of Amascut)
entries.detail: MOSTLY MODELLED, and the entry is kept for a narrower reason than it was written for. data/overrides/chest-tombs-of-amascut.json now models, wiki-verified in apps/ingest/test/toa.test.ts: the points-and-raid-level unique chance and its 55% cap (toa_invocation, matching the page's own worked example of 1% per 3,700 points at raid level 400), the raid-level-scaled 7-item unique pool including the out-of-invocation-range 1/50 (toa_unique_weight, reproducing all five rows of the page's published weight table from Module:Tombs of Amascut loot's own rule), the sub-1,500-point dung gate and its suppression of common rewards, the common table's points/divisor quantity scaling (toa_common_qty), the thread and jewel bad-luck-mitigation curves with their ownership reversions (toa_bad_luck_mitigation), the jewel pool's guarantee of an unowned jewel, the elite clue's 25% cap (toa_elite_clue) and the pet curve (toa_pet). What remains unmodelled, and why this stays watchlisted: the five remnant challenge rewards each require every invocation of one encounter set at level 4 (e.g. Remnant of akkha needs all Akkha invocations and level 4 Akkha) with zero party deaths, which is a per-raid invocation-composition fact no Condition kind expresses and no scalar can stand in for — drops_covered names exactly those five. Also out of scope: team size (this project's raid chests are all modelled per player, solo — a shared scope decision documented once in docs/DECISIONS.md's 'Raid loot is modelled per player, solo, everywhere' entry, not restated per source), the elite combat achievement's 1.05x clue multiplier, and duplicate jewels once all four are owned. Do not remove this entry to move the counter.

entries.title: Ancient chest
entries.detail: MOSTLY MODELLED; this entry is now stale in a narrower sense than when it was written and has been rechecked, not just re-read. data/overrides/ancient-chest.json (24 wiki-figure tests in apps/ingest/test/ancient-chest.test.ts) models the points-scaled unique roll (cox_points: up to six independent 570,000-point-capped rolls, 65.7% aggregate cap), the 33-slot common table's nested herb/seed oneOf pairs (preserves 'the two rolls cannot end on the same drop'), its points-driven QtySpec.formula quantities, and ownership gates on Dark journal/Ancient tablet the previously-generated document lacked entirely (it awarded Dark journal on every single kill). Two named residuals plus one shared scope decision keep it at 'approximate' rather than manual_override, none blocked on missing wiki text — rechecked this session, including a full re-read of Module:Chambers of Xeric calculator specifically (the same module that resolved ToA's and ToB's own 'unknown' constants), which does NOT hold the answer for either: (1) Ancient tablet's stated 'replaces one of the loot rolls' is modelled as an ADDITIONAL independent 1/10 roll instead — no run-scoped mechanism exists for one table's hit to reduce another table's roll count; a small, bounded, one-time overstatement (only until the account owns one), not a guess. (2) Metamorphic dust's 'if the raid was completed within a certain time' qualifier has no threshold stated anywhere. Module:Chambers of Xeric calculator's full text (re-checked) never touches tertiary rewards at all — Dark journal, Ancient tablet, Metamorphic dust and Twisted ancestral colour kit appear nowhere in it, its scope is strictly the unique/common EV tables. The wiki page's own raritynotes citation for this line is a 2018 developer Q&A YouTube timestamp, not a written number. Genuinely unstated, not a missed source this time — only the Challenge Mode gate is applied, which overstates true availability for a slow Challenge Mode clear. Also out of scope: per-player, not per-party (ctx.points stands in for the whole raid's points) — the shared, deliberate single-player scope decision documented once in docs/DECISIONS.md's 'Raid loot is modelled per player, solo, everywhere' entry, identical in shape to Tombs of Amascut's and Theatre of Blood's own chests, not restated in full here.

entries.title: Monumental chest
entries.detail: MOSTLY MODELLED — data/overrides/monumental-chest.json (22 wiki-figure tests in apps/ingest/test/monumental-chest.test.ts) models the points-scaled unique roll (tob_points: derived from roomsSkipped/deaths, matching Module:Theatre of Blood calculator's own solo-player playerpoints out of a 32-point max), the Normal/Hard Mode weight split, Hard Mode's stated 1.30x time-bonus multiplier (the module's own flat figure, not the page prose's compounding 1.15x1.15 reading), and the Cabbage/Message '0 individual contribution points' gate, which the previously-generated document fired on every single kill unconditionally. Three named residuals keep it at 'approximate': (1) team/party allocation — this player's own points stand in for the whole raid's, out of this simulator's single-player scope, the same shared decision as the other raid chests (see docs/DECISIONS.md's 'Raid loot is modelled per player, solo, everywhere' entry). (2) The 'individual performance' scaling on all five tertiary rates has no stated magnitude anywhere on the page — genuinely unknown, not modelled at all, same refusal-to-guess as elsewhere on this watchlist. (3) Entry Mode's prose-only common-table -80% is applied as a flat constant; whether it interacts with points/deaths the way Normal/Hard Mode do is unconfirmed either way, so nothing is guessed.

entries.title: Rewards Chest (Fortis Colosseum)
entries.detail: SHIPPED — data/overrides/rewards-chest-fortis-colosseum.json (14 wiki-figure tests in apps/ingest/test/rewards-chest-fortis-colosseum.test.ts). No Module:/Calculator: page exists for this source (checked directly); the 12 waves' published weighted tables ARE the complete source, each reconciling exactly to its own denominator, and ctx.wavesReached is selected by an ordinary levelAtLeast condition — no new formula was needed. What stays watchlisted: the 'guaranteed a full set before receiving duplicate Sunfire fanatic pieces' rule is shipped as a WITH-REPLACEMENT approximation (no ownershipGate), because whether that protection resets per Colosseum attempt or is a permanent account-wide guarantee is not stated anywhere checked — the armour and helm pages, the page's own full patch history, and three Jagex devblog mirrors from the release cycle, checked across two separate sessions, still unresolved either way. Quantified, not assumed small: the per-piece expected drop rate the simulator's headline numbers show is IDENTICAL under both models by symmetry; the cost is entirely in same-run joint statistics no headline number surfaces (P(a duplicate armour piece this run) ~0.20% under this approximation vs ~0.00025% true, an ~800x relative overstatement though both are absolute-tiny; P(a complete 3-piece set in one run) understated ~4.4x). If the protection turns out to be lifetime-scoped, an EXACT model via ownershipGate is directly available and should replace this approximation.
